theater: 全羅道全州與公州一線

battle.name: 東學黨起義
battle.theater: 全羅道全州與公州一線
battle.brief: 一八九四年春，東學黨在古府起事，四月集結數萬農民，連破正邑、黃土現，五月底攻入全州城。朝廷引清國兵入朝，日本亦以護僑為名出兵，清日聯軍以新式砲火在公州烏金峙一線擊潰義軍。一八九五年四月，全琯準於漢城被處斬；線膛砲代表的，是這場戰爭裡已嫌過時、仍留在朝鮮城頭的舊式前裝砲火。

kit.name: 線膛砲
kit.history: 線膛讓同樣的藥量走得更遠。砲兵第一次可以在射程上贏步兵。

countries: 交戰的一方是朝鮮王國朝廷及其軍隊。朝廷以漢城與各道的鎭管營、巡檢、束伍為骨幹，另行臨時募集義兵與地方官衙的雜色軍，指揮由高宗與閔氏一系的中央政府直落到各道觀察使。地方上的將領多為文官，如全羅兵馬節度使、義兵節制使、順無使與忠清監察使，砲兵集中在各道城營，兵員不多，但仍保有數門前裝洋砲可用。第二方是清國。一八九四年六月，應朝鮮國王之請，清廷派榆林軍自山東登陸入朝，記名軍與北洋各營續至，由湖南巡撫吳大澂統帶，駐漢城與平壤一線，裝備德製克虜伯後膛砲與大量淮軍式步槍，李鴻章在天津調度，駐朝鮮的袁世凱居中接應。第三方是日本。以保護本國僑民為由自六月出兵，初期只派數百人，平壤戰後大批增兵，至十一月公州一線已以大隊為單位作戰，並把新式步槍與機槍直接撥給朝鮮官軍。第四方是義軍，分三支：全羅與忠清南部的南接，領袖全琯準、金開男、孫和中；忠清北部的北接，領袖崔時亨與孫炳熙；忠清南部的西接，領袖施長玉。各部各有接主、大接主與參謀，互不統屬，糧餉與兵員就地自募，全軍沒有統一司令部。
countriesEn: The Korean side was the government of the Joseon dynasty together with its own troops. Its backbone was the garrisons of the capital and of each province, the patrol units and the local constables, supplemented by loyal volunteers raised on the spot and by the mixed bands that provincial offices could scrape together; command ran from King Gojong and the Min clan at the centre down to the provincial inspectors. The field commanders were mostly civil officials, such as the Jeolla Military Commissioner, the Commander of Loyal Volunteers, the Pacification Commissioner and the Chungcheong Inspector, and the artillery was concentrated in the provincial cities and camps: few in number, but they still had a handful of old muzzle-loading foreign guns to call on. The second side was Qing China. In June 1894, at the request of the Korean king, the court sent the Yulin Army over from Shandong, followed by units of the Jiming Army and the Beiyang formations, under the overall command of the Hunan governor Wu Dacheng, stationed on the Seoul and Pyongyang lines and equipped with German Krupp breech-loading guns and a large body of Huai-style rifles; Li Hongzhang directed the effort from Tianjin and Yuan Shikai handled the legation side in Korea. The third side was Japan. It sent troops from June on the stated ground of protecting its own nationals, at first only a few hundred men, and after the fall of Pyongyang in August it reinforced in force, so that by November on the Gongju line it was fighting by battalion and was handing modern rifles and machine guns straight to the Korean government troops. The fourth side was the rebel army, itself split three ways: the southern faction in Jeolla and southern Chungcheong under Jeon Bong-jun, Kim Gaenam and Son Hwagung; the northern faction in northern Chungcheong under Choe Si-hyeong and Son Byong-hui; and the western faction in southern Chungcheong under Seo Jang-ok. Each had its own chiefs, and none answered to a single command; men and grain were raised where they stood, and the whole army had no general headquarters at all.
people: 東學的創教人崔濟愚於一八六二年在江原道春川一帶立教，主張以博文與敬天修心為本，兼取儒、釋與巫俗。一八六四年壬午政變後朝廷大捕教眾，崔濟愚被處死，其弟崔濟安亦難倖免，教眾流入山區，漸成反抗政府的武裝團體，東學此後分裂為法派與西派之說。起義的直接指揮者是全琯準。他是南接的東道大將軍，出身樵戶與鄉紳之間，讀書不多而善寫文書，義軍的通文、檄文與〈全琯準供草〉都出自他手。他於一八九〇至一八九二年間曾出入興宣大院君門下，運動初期主張借大院君之力改革朝政，被拒後轉為排斥外勢的擁護者；一八九四年秋天日軍兵臨京城以後，他不再提擁立新王的話，改以斥倭為旗號，最後被俘，於一八九五年四月在漢城伏法。金開男是泰仁的大接主，革命派，堅持推翻現有政權；孫和中是溫和派，起義初期曾把全軍統制權交給全琯準，兩人之後屢起衝突。金開男在公州與烏金峙一線戰敗後被部下告密，押送全州途中被地方官員即決處死；孫和中與數名總參謀、總帥將則同全琯準一起伏法。北接領袖崔時亨始終以爭取傳教自由為先，起義失敗後仍留在民間傳教，是東學在後半世紀延續下來的關鍵人物，孫炳熙同樣脫身。朝廷一方的高宗在起義初期向清國求援，其後轉而倚重日本；親日派官僚金弘集在甲午改革中上位，把朝鮮內政推向日本。清國方面，吳大澂帶兵入朝，李鴻章在後方策應，聶士成的先鋒營與葉志成的第三鎮先後投入朝鮮戰場，前者在義軍與官軍的戰線外作戰，後者於同年九月在牙山被日軍打散，黃海海戰中丁汝昌戰死，清國在朝鮮的部署自此逐步收縮。日本方面，陸軍大臣山縣有馬推動出兵，伊藤博文以特使身分來朝；日本公使館的情報網截破興宣大院君與李埈永的政變計畫，義軍第二次舉事也因此被清廷與朝廷視為必須剷除的對象。
peopleEn: The founder of Donghak was Choe Je-u, who established the sect in the Cheolwon area of Gangwon in 1862, teaching universal love and a reverent cultivation of the mind, drawing on Confucian, Buddhist and shamanic elements at once. After the 1864 coup the court rounded the believers up on a mass scale, Choe Je-u was executed and his brother Choe Je-an did not survive either; the faithful took to the mountains and hardened into armed bands, and from that point Donghak split into a legal faction and a western faction. The man who actually directed the rising was Jeon Bong-jun. He was the East Commander-in-Chief of the southern faction, born between a charcoal burner and a local notable, with little schooling but a good hand at documents: the rebel circulars, the proclamations and the confession of Jeon Bong-jun all came from him. Between 1890 and 1892 he had moved in the circle of the Heungseon Daewongun, and in the first months of the movement he argued for using the Daewongun's influence to reform the court; when that was refused he turned to the rhetoric of driving out the foreign powers, and after the Japanese entered Seoul in the autumn of 1894 he dropped any talk of raising a new king, took up the banner of driving out the Japanese instead, and was finally taken alive and executed in Seoul in April 1895. Kim Gaenam was the chief of the Taein district and the hard-line leader who insisted on overthrowing the existing government; Son Hwagung was the moderate who handed overall control of the army to Jeon Bong-jun at the start of the rising, and the two clashed repeatedly afterwards. Kim Gaenam was betrayed by one of his own men after the defeat on the Gongju and Uigumchi line and was summarily executed by a provincial officer while being taken to Jeonju; Son Hwagung and the chief of staff and the chief marshal of the army were shot with Jeon Bong-jun. Choe Si-hyeong, the head of the northern faction, cared throughout about winning freedom of religion rather than about the rising itself, and stayed in the country afterwards to keep preaching, which is why Donghak survived into the second half of the century; Son Byong-hui escaped as well. On the government side King Gojong asked Qing China for help in the first months and then leaned on Japan instead; Kim Hong-jip, the pro-Japanese minister, rose during the Gabo reform and steered Korean internal affairs towards Japan. On the Qing side Wu Dacheng brought the army into the country, Li Hongzhang directed matters from the north, the advance contingent of Nie Shicheng and Ye Zhicheng's third brigade were committed to Korea in turn, the former fighting outside the rebel-government line and the latter broken by the Japanese at Asan in September of the same year; Ding Ruchang was killed in the Battle of the Yellow Sea, and the Qing deployment in Korea contracted from that point on. On the Japanese side the Army Minister Yamagata Aritomo pressed for the deployment, Ito Hirobumi came to Korea as special envoy, and the legation intelligence network uncovered the coup plot of the Heungseon Daewongun and Yi Jun-yong, which is why the second rising of the rebels was thereafter treated by the Qing court and the Korean government as something that had to be crushed.
kits: 卡面這件兵器是一八五〇年的德製線膛前裝野戰砲。線膛把同樣份量的火藥壓進一條不漏氣的螺旋溝裡，藥力因此用在彈丸上而不是從炮膛壁白白漏掉，射程比同口徑滑膛砲遠了一大截，砲兵第一次可以在射程上贏過步兵。一八九四年的朝鮮戰場上，這門技術確實還在場上，只是已經站在舊與新的分界線上。朝鮮官軍的砲兵人數一向稀少，砲卻還有：各道兵馬節度使衙門與城營裡存著一八六〇年代至七〇年代購置的前裝洋砲，其中線膛前裝砲口徑較大、射程較滑膛砲為遠。黃土現至完山一線的官軍正是靠這種砲火壓制義軍，義軍只有獵槍、火繩槍與死鐮，望不見對面的人就已被打得全線後退，一次戰役折損數百人；義軍入全州城之後才從城內兵器庫與徵集所得中取得火炮，清點下來只有兩門砲、一百餘支槍，多是火繩槍與天保槍一類的舊式前裝槍。真正決定後段戰局的是新式武器：十一月公州一線，朝鮮官軍經日本之手配到德製克虜伯後膛砲、加特林機槍、英國斯奈德步槍與日本自製的村田步槍，清朝入朝的榆林軍同樣用德製後膛砲。線膛前裝砲與後膛砲之間的差距，不只是射程，還有射速、精度與彈藥供應，後膛砲可以臥姿連發，義軍的舊砲只能點放；烏金峙一線，日軍的機槍與砲火在百五十米外把攻上山脊的義軍壓住，義軍用盡全力也未能突破，前一日效砲的戰鬥中義軍還丟掉了那兩門砲。義軍自身的裝備更原始：第一次起事時是死鐮、鋤頭、長矛與弓箭，頭上綁白布；其後繳獲官軍的槍械與少量火器，第三次起事時仍以火繩槍、獵槍、弓矢與長槍為主。糧食靠徵收與就地向農戶徵發，運輸靠人力揹運與牛車，攻城靠夜襲、攀城與火攻，全無攻城砲與重砲；官軍這一邊有騎兵、工兵、醫療兵與電信，也有能遠程調動的砲兵部隊。線膛砲在這場戰爭裡真正扮演的角色，是義軍從無砲到有砲的門檻，而不是勝負的關鍵。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is a German rifled muzzle-loading field gun of 1850. Rifling forces the same charge of powder into a spiral groove that does not leak, so the energy goes into the shot instead of bleeding away through the wall of the bore, and the range is far greater than that of a smoothbore of the same calibre: artillery could beat infantry on range for the first time. The technology was genuinely still on the field in Korea in 1894, though it stood right on the line between the old and the new. The Korean government had always had few gunners, but it did have guns: the offices of the provincial military commissioners and the city garrisons held muzzle-loading foreign guns bought in the 1860s and 1870s, among them rifled muzzle-loaders of larger bore and longer range than the smoothbores. At the line from Huangtuxian to Wansan the government army leaned on exactly that artillery fire to pin the rebels, who had only hunting guns, matchlocks and dead sickles, could not even see the enemy, and were driven back along the whole line with several hundred men lost in a single action. Only after they entered Jeonju did the rebels pick up guns, from the city arsenal and from requisition; the count came to two cannon and a little over a hundred firearms, mostly matchlocks and old muzzleloaders of the Tianbao type. What really decided the later stage was the new equipment. On the Gongju line in November the Korean government troops, armed through Japan, had German Krupp breech-loaders, Gatling machine guns, British Snider rifles and the Japanese Murata rifle, while the Qing Yulin Army that had entered Korea likewise brought German breech-loading guns. The gap between a rifled muzzleloader and a breech-loader was not only range: it was rate of fire, accuracy and ammunition supply, because a breech-loader could fire lying down while the old gun could only fire single shots. At Uigumchi the Japanese machine guns and artillery poured fire onto the rebels from a hundred and fifty metres away and held them on the ridge, and the rebels never got through; the day before, at Hyop'o, they had already lost both of their cannon. The rebels' own equipment was more primitive still: at the first rising they had dead sickles, hoes, spears and bows, with white cloth tied round their heads; later they picked up government firearms and a few weapons, and by the third rising they were still mainly armed with matchlocks, hunting guns, arrows and spears. Food was taken by requisition and by levying on the villages on the spot, transport was by human carriers and ox carts, and sieges were done by night attack, scaling and fire: there was no siege gun and no heavy artillery anywhere in the rebel army. On the government side there were cavalry, engineers, medical staff and the telegraph, and artillery formations that could be shifted over distance. The part the rifled field gun really played in this war was the threshold between a rebel army with no cannon and one with two; it was not the hinge of the outcome.
tactics: 義軍的打法有前後兩段，分野在於有沒有砲。第一次起事靠的是集會式的閃擊：一八九四年二月十五日，數百名農民在古府馬目場集結，頭上綁白布，手持死鐮與農具，一路由夜行四十里摸到郡衙，破了武庫，奪了兵器，把非法徵收的糧食分給農戶，然後在新任郡守到任後自行解散。第二次起事轉為有組織的進攻：全琯準在栢山一帶設總部，發布四大名義與十二條紀律，設東道大將軍、總管令、總參謀、總帥將與祕書等職，進行基本軍事訓練，再以每郡為單位同時起事，佔領正邑、興德與高昌後轉戰黃土現與黃龍村，五月三十一日攻入全州城，攻城靠的是夜襲與縱火，而不是正面強攻。全州佔領之後，義軍做了一件在亞洲史上罕見的事：同政府談判。六月十一日簽訂全州和約，以二十七條要求換取義軍撤出與設立農民議事所，全羅道五十三個郡一時出現農民自設的議事與行政機關。這次成功的政治操作沒有配合軍事勝利，義軍散去，武器散落各村。第三次起事已經換了目標：八月日軍攻破平壤，九月義軍在王城一帶重新集結，旗號由改革變成斥倭，路線分成三路，全琯準取公州、水原至漢城，金開男取金山、清州至漢城，北接在論山會合。義軍沿途切斷日軍的電信，襲擊兵站與後勤車隊，試圖用速度與縱深把日軍拖垮，但缺乏統一指揮，各部各打各的。公州一線的戰術仍是人多勢眾式的密集攻山：以兩路佯攻牽制守軍，主力沿狹窄的烏金峙山道仰攻，結果在百五十米外就被機槍與砲火壓住，一週之內發動四十餘次衝鋒而不能登頂。官軍的戰術正好相反：以砲火與射界換傷亡，不與義軍在平地糾纏，佔住狹窄路口與高地，兵力雖只數千卻能反覆出擊；義軍潰散後，搜捕與懸賞同步進行，義軍首腦多在部下告密下被捕。線膛砲的射程在這裡成了官軍的繩索：不靠近，只用砲火把對方從山脊上壓下來。
tacticsEn: The rebels fought in two manners, and the dividing line was whether they had cannon. The first rising was a massed rush: on 15 February 1894 several hundred peasants assembled at the horse market of Gobu with white cloth on their heads, carrying dead sickles and farm tools, marched forty li through the night to fall on the county office, broke the armoury, took the weapons and gave out grain that had been levied illegally, and then dispersed of their own accord once a new magistrate arrived. The second rising became an organised offensive: Jeon Bong-jun set up a headquarters in the Paeksan area, proclaimed the four great principles and the twelve rules of discipline, created the posts of East Commander-in-Chief, Director-General, Chief of Staff, Chief Marshal and Secretary, and drilled the men in the elements of military life, and then had every district rise on the same day; after taking Jeonp'yong, Hungdok and Koch'ang they fought at Huangtuxian and Hwangryongch'on, and on 31 May they entered the city of Jeonju, not by frontal assault but by night attack and by fire. Having taken Jeonju the rebels did something rare in Asian history: they negotiated with the government. On 11 June the Jeonju compact was signed, twenty-seven conditions being exchanged for a rebel withdrawal and for the setting up of local assemblies, and for a time fifty-three districts of Jeolla had peasant-run councils and administrations of their own. That political success was not matched by any military one; the rebels dispersed and their weapons scattered among the villages. The third rising had changed its aim: after the Japanese took Pyongyang in August, the rebels mustered again around the capital in September, the banner changed from reform to driving out the Japanese, and the march split into three prongs, Jeon Bong-jun taking Gongju and Suwon on the road to Seoul, Kim Gaenam taking Geumsan and Cheongju on the road to Seoul, the northern faction joining at Nonsan. On the way the rebels cut the Japanese telegraph, raided the depots and the baggage trains, hoping to wear the Japanese down with speed and depth, but with no unified command each contingent fought its own war. The method on the Gongju line was still the massed assault up a hill: two feints to distract the defence while the main body tried to climb the narrow path at Uigumchi, only to be pinned down by machine-gun and artillery fire from a hundred and fifty metres away, and to fail in more than forty separate attacks over the course of a week. The government fought the exact opposite way: it traded casualties for firepower and fields of fire rather than wrestling with the rebels in the open, held the narrow passes and the high ground, and though it had only a few thousand men it could attack again and again; once the rebels broke, the searching parties and the posted rewards went out together, and most of the rebel leaders were picked up because their own men informed on them. Here the reach of the rifled field gun became the government's rope: never come close, and simply press the enemy off the ridge with gunpowder.
data: 時間線可以排得很清楚：一八九四年二月十五日第一次起事於古府，四月第二次起事，五月三十一日攻入全州，六月十一日簽訂全州和約，九月第三次起事，十一月二十日至十二月七日公州一線決戰，一八九五年四月二十三日首腦伏法，自爆發到收場共十四個月。人數方面各方記載出入很大。義軍第二次起事時聲稱在栢山集結一萬人，實際投入前線者以數千計；黃土現之役朝廷派出的全羅監察與營官率領雜色軍約一萬人，義軍先以火器擾亂其陣腳再行追擊，一名營官被擒殺。第三次起事的總數，官方百科記南北兩集合兵近四萬人，義軍自稱二十萬，能核實的是論山會師時南北各約一萬、合計兩萬餘人，其中全琯準能直接調動的約一萬，攻公州的先鋒四千；烏金峙總攻時投入約兩萬。官軍一方，順無使以下各鎮共三千二百人，日軍以兩個大隊支援，另有一說只派數百人；守住烏金峙路口的官軍約九百八十人。傷亡方面，黃土現之役官軍折損數百，完山一線義軍因無法反砲而戰死者約五百；效砲之役義軍死七十餘人並丟失兩門砲；烏金峙一週四十餘次衝鋒，官軍死一百二十餘人、傷三百餘人；義軍最後在金邱院坪一帶只餘五百餘人，潰散後被追殺者無數。武器方面，義軍攻入全州時只有兩門砲與一百餘支槍，其後在圍剿中耗散殆盡。距離與天候同樣要緊：古府、正邑、全州與光州分佈在漢城西南二百至三百公里，義軍靠步行與牛車移動，走完全州至公州約七十公里；三月插秧與五月農忙抽走大量青壯，四月出兵的兵源因此吃緊；六月梅雨與九月颱風都使糧秣與彈藥的運送遲滯，十一月以後南部山區轉冷、江面結冰，義軍原本指望清國出兵與天時，等來的卻是官軍的搜捕。
dataEn: The chronology can be laid out cleanly: the first rising at Gobu on 15 February 1894, the second rising in April, the entry into Jeonju on 31 May, the Jeonju compact signed on 11 June, the third rising in September, the decisive fighting on the Gongju line from 20 November to 7 December, and the execution of the leaders on 23 April 1895, fourteen months from outbreak to finish. The numbers are disputed and the records differ. At the second rising the rebels claimed ten thousand gathered at Paeksan, and the number actually committed to the front was in the thousands; at the battle of Huangtuxian the court sent its Jeolla inspector and camp commander with about ten thousand men of the miscellaneous levies, and the rebels disrupted them with gunfire before charging, and a camp commander was taken and killed. For the third rising the official encyclopedia puts the northern and southern combined force at close to forty thousand, the rebels themselves claimed two hundred thousand, and what can be checked is that at the junction at Nonsan each wing numbered about ten thousand, twenty thousand or more in all, of which Jeon Bong-jun could personally call on perhaps ten thousand and the assault column for Gongju was four thousand; about twenty thousand were committed to the general attack at Uigumchi. On the government side the forces under the Pacification Commissioner and the provincial commands totalled 3,200 men, with two Japanese battalions in support, though one account puts the Japanese at only several hundred; the government troops actually holding the pass at Uigumchi numbered about 980. On losses: several hundred government men fell at Huangtuxian; at the Wansan line the rebels lost about five hundred dead because they had no guns to answer the artillery; at Hyop'o they lost over seventy dead and both of their cannon; in the more than forty attacks over a week at Uigumchi the government lost some 120 dead and 300 wounded; the rebels were down to about five hundred men around the Wonpyeong plateau in Geumgu, and many more were killed in the pursuit. In matériel the rebels had only two cannon and a little over a hundred firearms when they entered Jeonju, and those were ground down during the suppression that followed. Distance and weather mattered as much: Gobu, Jeongeup, Jeonju and Gwangju lie between two hundred and three hundred kilometres south-west of Seoul, and the rebels moved on foot and on ox carts, about seventy kilometres from Jeonju to Gongju; the March transplanting and the May harvest took away strong arms, which is why the April levy of men was thin; the June rains and the September typhoons held up the movement of grain and powder; and after November the mountains of the south turned cold and the rivers iced over, and the rebels who had counted on Qing intervention and on the season instead got the government search parties.
cause: 起義有兩層根子，表面的導火線在朝鮮朝廷，深處的根子在東學教本身與三十年的山區抗爭。直接導火線是一八九二年到任的全羅道古府郡守的橫暴。朝鮮末期的郡府制度靠常例與各種雜稅維持，官吏下鄉巡查時任意徵收，民間早已怨聲載道；東學教眾聚居山區，半農半教，遇上郡吏入鄉搜查教眾，衝突便不可避免。第一次起事在郡衙被攻破後自行解散，但朝廷派來按覈使的安撫只答應懲罰官吏，沒有觸及制度，於是義軍再起。第二層根子在教派自身。一八六四年崔濟愚被處死後，東學在十年之間被壓成三支不同的武裝團體：法派以崔時亨一系為主，只求傳教自由；西派以施長玉為主；南接則是在洪州、泰安、正邑一帶山民與佃農的基礎上長出來，把教義同鄉土矛盾綁在一起，主張廢除均田使、廢除名目稅、改善奴婢與七種賤民的待遇。這些主張遠超同時代實學家與開化派能提出的範圍，使朝廷既不能接受，也無法用一句安撫了事。外部條件同樣重要：一八九〇年代清日兩國在朝鮮的角力已到臨界點，日本依一八八五年條約取得在朝駐兵權並加速滲透，清國靠袁世凱把持朝鮮的商務與外交，朝廷自身既無兵又無財，只好借外力壓內亂；而興宣大院君一系正想利用這場亂局擁立其孫李埈永，日本公使館的情報網一旦截破這條線，義軍第二次舉事便從朝政改革的題目，變成國際較量的棋子。
causeEn: The rising had two sets of roots: on the surface a spark in the Korean court, and underneath the sect itself and thirty years of resistance in the mountains. The immediate spark was the conduct of the magistrate of Gobu in Jeolla, who took office in 1892. The late Joseon district administration was kept going by customary dues and a great many irregular levies, and officials travelling through the countryside levied as they pleased, to the anger of the population. The Donghak faithful lived in the mountains, farming half the year and preaching the other half, and when a district officer came into the villages to search for believers, the collision was inevitable. The first rising dissolved by itself once the county office had been taken, but the pacification commissioner the court sent down promised only to punish the officials and did not touch the system, and the rebels rose again. The second set of roots lies in the sect. After Choe Je-u was executed in 1864, Donghak was compressed within ten years into three different armed groups: the legal faction under Choe Si-hyeong's line wanted only freedom to preach; the western faction followed Seo Jang-ok; the southern faction grew out of the mountain folk and tenants around Hongju, Taein and Jeongeup and bound the doctrine to local grievances, demanding the abolition of the land-equalising office, of the irregular taxes, and better treatment for slaves and the seven kinds of despised people. These demands ran well past anything the real scholars and the reform party of the day could have proposed, and left the court unable either to accept them or to settle the matter with a single soothing phrase. The external conditions were equally important: by the 1890s the Sino-Japanese rivalry in Korea had reached a breaking point, Japan had won the right to station troops under the treaty of 1885 and was pressing in, the Qing court held the commerce and the diplomacy of the peninsula through Yuan Shikai, and the Korean government, with neither soldiers nor money of its own, could only borrow outside force to put down internal disorder. At the same time the Heungseon Daewongun's circle wanted to use the disturbance to put his grandson Yi Jun-yong on the throne, and once the legation intelligence network cut that thread, the second rising of the rebels turned from a question of court reform into a piece on the board of international rivalry.
impact: 這場起義的影響，一半在朝鮮內部，一半在東亞。對朝鮮來說，農民武裝第一次以農民議事所的形式在自己的村落裡運作，全羅道五十三個郡一度出現農民自設的議事與行政機關，其綱領包括廢除名目稅、廢除均田使、改善奴婢與七種賤民的待遇，雖然很快被鎮壓，但此後韓國的農民運動與開化運動都反覆回到這批要求上。東學教本身沒有消失：一八九八年由崔永勳改組為天道教，一九一五年再與眞友會、觀音道合併為卍字會，今天仍是韓國在世的宗教之一。起義之後，朝鮮的政治走向被外力接管：一八九四年七月日本軍隊擅自進入景福宮並迫使朝廷接受改革要求，甲午改革由校正廳與軍國機務處推行，親日派官僚上位；翌年日本又製造乙未事變。到一九〇五年設統監府、一九一〇年合併，朝鮮作為自主國家的最後一點制度外衣被剝掉，而引爆這條連鎖的，正是這場農民起義。在國際層面，這場起義是甲午戰爭的直接導火線：清日兩國都以朝鮮內亂為由出兵，戰爭的勝負反過來決定了朝鮮的命運。中國在黃海海戰以及平壤、遼陽一線的失利，使朝鮮的宗藩關係徹底斷裂；而東亞各國由此看清了一件事，近代式砲兵與後膛速射武器已經可以決定遠東的秩序，日本此後十年間在朝鮮與大陸上的推進，正是建立在這次較量之上。歷史記憶方面，韓國在一九九〇年代把事件名稱統一為「東學農民革命」，其後就流傳的「十二條改革綱領」的真偽展開長達數十年的史實查明，官方認定其並非史實；一九九四年百週年時，學界重新確認了這場起義在韓國近代史上作為農民政治運動的地位。
impactEn: The effects of the rising fell half inside Korea and half across East Asia. For Korea, it was the first time an armed peasant movement ran its own affairs inside its own villages through the local assemblies: for a time fifty-three districts of Jeolla had peasant-run councils and administrations, with a programme that included abolishing the irregular taxes, abolishing the land-equalising office and bettering the condition of slaves and the seven despised groups. It was suppressed quickly, but the demands it raised came back again and again in the later peasant and reform movements of the country. Donghak itself did not disappear: it was reorganised as Cheondoism by Choi Yeong-hun in 1898, and in 1915 it was merged with the Jinuhoe and the Gwaneumdo into the Wanjihoe, and it is still a living religion in Korea today. After the rising the political direction of the peninsula was taken over from outside: in July 1894 Japanese troops entered Gyeongbokgung without leave and forced the court to accept reform demands, the Gabo reform was carried through the Kyoseongcheong, the bureau created to correct the government, and the Gun-guk Gimucheo, the ministry of state affairs, and pro-Japanese ministers rose; the following year the Eulmi Incident was manufactured in Japan. With the Resident-General in 1905 and annexation in 1910, the last institutional covering of Korea's sovereignty was stripped away, and what set that chain in motion was this peasant rising. At the international level the rising was the direct trigger of the Sino-Japanese War: both China and Japan sent troops on the ground of the Korean unrest, and the result of the war decided the fate of Korea in turn. China's defeat in the Battle of the Yellow Sea and on the Pyongyang and Liaoyang lines severed the tributary relationship between Korea and China for good, and the states of East Asia could see clearly from it that modern artillery and breech-loading rapid-fire weapons could now decide the order of the Far East; the Japanese advance in Korea and on the continent over the following ten years rested on that demonstration. In terms of historical memory, Korea unified the name of the event as the Donghak Peasant Revolution in the 1990s, and the truth or falsehood of the circulated twelve-point reform programme was then argued for years in a fact-finding inquiry that officially found no such document to have existed; at the centenary in 1994 scholarship re-established the rising's standing as a peasant political movement in modern Korean history.
result: 一八九四年十一月二十日至十二月七日，公州烏金峙一線打了兩個星期。義軍在效砲一役先失兩門砲，烏金峙一週四十餘次衝鋒又被機槍與砲火壓回，十二月十日再遭夜襲，義軍退回論山與全州，在元坪與泰仁一線的最後一戰仍告失敗。全琯準下令解散隊伍，只留直屬親兵，隨後在正邑與順昌之間流竄，十二月二十八日被自己的舊部告密擒獲，押送漢城，先移交日本公使館，再交法務衙門，自一八九五年三月五日至四月四日受審五次。審問中他始終否認與興宣大院君的關係，也沒有供出任何同黨姓名，只反覆申述自己的政治構想：驅逐日軍、逐出惡吏、與數名賢士共理國事，之後回到田間務農。一八九五年四月二十三日，裁判官宣判，全琯準、孫和中與數名總參謀、總帥將同時伏法；金開男在押送全州途中被地方官員即決處死。北接領袖崔時亨與孫炳熙在安撫其餘黨眾後得以倖存，東學教則作為宗教共同體在民間延續。從軍事結果看，義軍輸了：二十萬的口號、兩萬的實力、兩門砲、三週的強攻，換不回一個據點，而官軍與日軍在公州一線的損失不過數百人。從政治結果看，義軍同樣輸了：全州和約的二十七條要求，最後只換來一個被日本改寫過的甲午改革，農民自設的農民議事所被解散，朝鮮朝廷從此倚日制清。但戰爭並非全無收穫。東學教從一八九〇年代起再未消失，農民武裝起義在朝鮮此後的歷史裡屢次重現，一八九八年的三人浦事件與一九一〇至一九一九年間的各地農民運動都以此為旗號；一九二〇年代日本殖民當局在朝鮮中部山區的討伐戰，使用的正是這場起義留下的裝備與記憶。而一九九四年到一九九六年的史實查明，則把這場起義重新放回韓國國民記憶的中心位置。
resultEn: From 20 November to 7 December 1894 the fighting on the Gongju line at Uigumchi lasted two weeks. The rebels lost both cannon at Hyop'o, were driven back from Uigumchi by machine guns and artillery after more than forty attacks in a week, and were hit again by a night attack on 10 December, falling back through Nonsan to Jeonju and fighting their last engagement on the Wonpyeong and Taein line without success. Jeon Bong-jun ordered the army to disband and kept only his personal guard, moved about between Jeongeup and Sunchang, and on 28 December was taken by one of his own former followers and taken to Seoul, first to the Japanese legation and then to the Board of Justice, where he was interrogated five times between 5 March and 4 April 1895. Under examination he flatly denied any connection with the Heungseon Daewongun and gave up no name of any associate, and only restated his own political idea: drive the Japanese soldiers out, cast out the evil officials, govern the country jointly with a few worthy men, and then go back to the fields and farm. On 23 April 1895 the judges pronounced sentence, and Jeon Bong-jun, Son Hwagung and several of his staff were shot together; Kim Gaenam was summarily executed by a provincial officer on the road to Jeonju. Choe Si-hyeong and Son Byong-hui of the northern faction survived after gathering in the remaining followers, and Donghak carried on in the villages as a religious community. Militarily the rebels lost: two hundred thousand claimed on the banners, twenty thousand in fact, two cannon and three weeks of attacking bought not one position, while the government and Japanese at Gongju lost only several hundred men. Politically they lost as well: the twenty-seven conditions of the Jeonju compact ended by producing a Gabo reform rewritten by Japan, the peasant assemblies were dissolved, and the Korean court from then on governed under Japanese and Qing protection. Yet the war was not without yield. Donghak did not disappear again after the 1890s, armed peasant risings recurred in later Korean history under its banner, from the Saminpo incident of 1898 to the peasant movements of 1910 to 1919; and the suppression campaigns the Japanese colonial authorities fought in the central Korean mountains in the 1920s used the arms and the memory left behind by this rising. The fact-finding inquiry of 1994 to 1996 then put the rising back at the centre of Korean national memory.
